headline: Authors report poisoned-claim uptake under surprise-based continual learning
summary: A new preprint reports that surprise-only continual learning does not filter poisoned claims in controlled streams and can absorb most presented lies, including nearly all counterfactual lies about facts a model already knows. The study evaluates Qwen2.5-1.5B, Qwen2.5-3B and Llama-3.2-3B with atomic factual claims, invented entities and CounterFact examples. The authors report that a prior-conflict filter reduces some known-fact lies but blocks many legitimate updates; a source-evidence route helps only under assumptions about source integrity. These are author-reported small-model results, not independent or deployment-scale validation.
